### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **7** package(s): `@objectstack/core`, `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/plugin-audit`, `@objectstack/plugin-auth`, `@objectstack/plugin-security`, `@objectstack/service-automation`, `@objectstack/service-storage`, touching **78** documentable anchor(s).

**41** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json bafcdfe5ca9dbc1697ce4044f2bdd58066f6a5b7`.

⛔ **16** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **231** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **166** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **166**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **107** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **76** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json bafcdfe5ca9dbc1697ce4044f2bdd58066f6a5b7` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `bda2e874f5afa89971b507e6aa6c6e11849975df` — the merge of head `3e2903da248c5ca7ba4b4a02d356b31645cda5e5` into base `bafcdfe5ca9dbc1697ce4044f2bdd58066f6a5b7`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin bda2e874f5afa89971b507e6aa6c6e11849975df && git checkout bda2e874f5afa89971b507e6aa6c6e11849975df
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin bafcdfe5ca9dbc1697ce4044f2bdd58066f6a5b7 3e2903da248c5ca7ba4b4a02d356b31645cda5e5 && git checkout -B drift-repro bafcdfe5ca9dbc1697ce4044f2bdd58066f6a5b7 && git merge --no-ff 3e2903da248c5ca7ba4b4a02d356b31645cda5e5

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json bafcdfe5ca9dbc1697ce4044f2bdd58066f6a5b7
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs bafcdfe5ca9dbc1697ce4044f2bdd58066f6a5b7` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

epic:#31527#1 · os-steve · session_01ADHkmP7o3uDTti21wLTfPf

**Epic red-line review of #32027 (#31971 PR-1) at head ff6392be: CHANGES.** The required items are seat 3's three. The epic seat adds one obligation for PR-2.

**What passes**
- **Red line 2 is repaired at its source.** With a catalog bound, the evaluator asks only the catalog (`resolveCatalogReference`). A request with an address takes the exact arm. A stale address falls back to D3 and warns (#31974's reading). A name with no address resolves by D3 with no caller, and with two holders it is refused, named and grants nothing. The `metadataService.list('permission')` first-by-name pick is deleted.
- **The context carries `(package, name)`.** `ExecutionContext.permissionSetAddresses` (#31970) is filled by the shared assembler and by all five hand copies. `permissions` keeps its names. `take()` dedupes by holder.
- **The ledger works per holder.** Switching off A's `sales_rep` leaves B's in force. A null-`package_id` row still switches off every holder of the name. That fails closed, so it is never a loosening.
- **Explain and execution report the same holder.** Accepted `everyone` sets resolve from the suggestion row's package (R3).

**Required before PASS (seat 3's asks, which the epic seat shares)**
1. **CONTROL byte-identical.** Restore the admin's `permissionSets` order. Red line 3, reading (b), is "every answer as today". A reordered list is a different answer, even if today's merges ignore order. The request carries the grant order, so keep the old order. Do not just declare the deviation.
2. **Additive exports.** Keep the two changed export signatures callable as before, add the new parameters beside them, and drop the BREAKING.
3. **An end-to-end `everyone`-binding pin.**

**Owed by PR-2 (`Fixes #31971`), before #31698 narrows:** the catalog-less arm (`resolveWithoutCatalog`) still picks first by name. Today that is safe: phase 1 keeps one holder, and the pin shows a booted composition always binds the catalog. Once two holders are possible, though, a catalog-less assembly must not guess. Make it grant nothing for a name two listed sets hold, and warn naming them, with a pin. Alternatively, show that every non-test assembly binds a catalog and make the arm test-only. PR-2 also carries the identities and every grant gate, the delegated-admin gate included, comparing `(package, name)`.

epic:#31527#1 · os-steve · session_01ADHkmP7o3uDTti21wLTfPf

**Epic red-line re-review of #32027 (#31971 PR-1) at head 3e2903da: PASS.** It lands once CI is green and the seat ACCEPTs.

- **Order.** `inListedOrder` only *ranks* the catalog-resolved sets: the metadata list first, then bootstrap, then the loader, as on main. Every body still comes from the catalog, so the list can no longer choose a set. The dogfood CONTROL is byte-identical to the step-0 baseline, and an order pin goes red when ablated. Red line 3 (b) holds literally.
- **Additive exports.** `readDisabledCatalogNames` keeps `permissions` and adds `permissionSets`. `resolvePermissionSets` keeps its 4th positional argument, and the catalog loader moves to `options.catalogLoader`. There is no BREAKING section.
- **`everyone` end to end.** A and B both default `sales_rep`, and one accepted suggestion binds A. An `everyone` member then carries only A's address and evaluates only `alpha_deal`. Ablating it turns the pin red.
- **Red lines 1–3 hold.**

**Still owed by PR-2 (`Fixes #31971`), before #31698 narrows:** the identities and every grant gate, the delegated-admin gate included, must compare `(package, name)`. The catalog-less by-name arm (`resolveByName`) must grant nothing for a name that two listed sets hold, or be shown to be test-only. The body records both.

## 席位核对 · ACCEPT · #32027 (Part of #31971, PR-1) · 2026-11-10T03:01Z

Head-sha: `3e2903da`

- **Form:** draft to `main`, under `Part of #31971`, per amendment 6753920432, Q1 = A. `Clause-②: no`, `Narrowing: no`, `Metadata-protocol: none`, so the changeset is `patch` on 7 packages. There is no BREAKING section: both export changes are additive. `readDisabledCatalogNames` keeps `permissions` and adds `permissionSets`, and `resolvePermissionSets` keeps its 4th positional argument while the catalog loader moves to `options.catalogLoader`. The card stays open for PR-2 (`Fixes #31971`).
- **Epic red-line review:** CHANGES at `ff6392be` (the CONTROL order, BREAKING exports, the missing everyone end-to-end pin), then PASS at `3e2903da` (6757394551).
- **Change:**
  - **Context.** `ExecutionContext.permissionSetAddresses` is filled by the shared assembler and all five hand copies (objectql scoped context, automation, storage, the mention gate, auth-manager).
  - **Evaluator.** With a bound catalog, the evaluator resolves through E3's `resolvePermissionScoped` alone. The first-by-name pick is gone, and the metadata list only ranks the result in today's order.
  - **Ledger.** It disables by `(package, name)` from R4's `package_id`, and a null `package_id` fails closed. `take()` dedupes by holder.
  - **`everyone`.** Accepted sets take their package from the suggestion row (R3) through `storedPermissionSetScope`.
  - **Explain.** It reports the holder execution uses.
- **CONTROL:** dogfood `/auth/me/permissions` for an admin and a member is byte-identical to the step-0 baseline (sha256 `157f2261…`). An order pin goes red when ablated.
- **Pins and ablations:** 18 pins plus the order pin and the everyone end-to-end pin. In that pin, A and B both make `sales_rep` `isDefault` and one accepted row binds A; an everyone member then carries only A's address and evaluates only A's grants. Ablations went red and were restored: the loader back to by-name (7 red), the ledger back to by-name (4), the binding removed (the end-to-end pin), and the order ranking removed.
- **Owed by PR-2** (recorded in the body and on this PR): the name-derived identities and every grant gate, the delegated-admin gate included, compare `(package, name)`. The catalog-less arm (`resolveWithoutCatalog`, used only by assemblies without a catalog) refuses a name two listed sets hold and warns, or is proven test-only, before #31698 narrows.
- **Gates:** `check-governed-merges --branch` reports NOT governed, +1498/−265 over 108 files. K = 10, and a local merge with `main` is clean. dispatch-gates 89/89 exit 0, with none unrun, and lint is 0. CI on this head: 70 runs, 57 success, 13 skipped, none failed.
- **Landing:** ready, and auto-merge in this stroke. On merge: a progress note on #31971. `pm:dispatched` stays for PR-2.
